key_insight: Q-GAIN is a modular Python package that unifies machine learning and physics-informed analysis for rapid feature detection in cold-atom experiments.
engineering_relevance: It provides a reusable workflow for deploying classification, object detection, and physics-based metrics on experimental Bose-Einstein condensate data.
method: Build a pipeline from data loading and preprocessing to ML-based feature identification and conventional post-analysis.
Support multiple tasks out of the box, including classification, object detection, and physics-informed metrics.
Demonstrate flexibility through MNIST digit classification, soliton detection, and vortex detection in ring-shaped BEC images.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports three demonstration applications: MNIST classification, reimplementation of SolDet for soliton detection in time-of-flight data, and object detection of quantized vortices in ring-shaped BEC images.
watch_item: Performance and robustness may depend on careful task-specific preprocessing and integration with experimental imaging conditions.
paper_title: Q-GAIN: A Python Package for Machine Learning and Physically Informed Analysis Applications
